branding.tagline: Build a world that outlives you.

jobs.name: Foraging
jobs.description: Gather berries, roots and small game.

jobs.name: Farming
jobs.description: Sow, tend and harvest the fields. Depends on the season.

jobs.name: Wood Gathering
jobs.description: Collect deadwood and fell small trees.

jobs.name: Crafting
jobs.description: Turn wood and stone into tools that make all gatherers faster.

jobs.name: Research
jobs.description: Elders share and test ideas, producing knowledge.

jobs.name: Fishing
jobs.description: Cast lines and traps in the river and the lake.

jobs.name: Hunting
jobs.description: Track deer and boar in the forest. Brings meat and hides.

jobs.name: Mining
jobs.description: Dig ore from the veins at the foot of the mountains.

seasons.name: Spring
seasons.description: Fields can be sown and the community grows.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.description: Berries ripen and the days are long.

seasons.name: Autumn
seasons.description: Harvest time: fill the stores and the woodpile before winter.

seasons.name: Winter
seasons.description: Wild food is scarce and every hearth burns firewood.

buildings.name: Campfire
buildings.description: The heart of the camp. Elders gather here to share knowledge.

buildings.name: Shelter
buildings.description: A hide tent on a ring of poles. Houses 2 people.

buildings.name: Woven Shelter
buildings.description: Woven walls on a stone base. Houses 4 people.

buildings.name: Foraging Camp
buildings.description: A base for food gatherers. +3 Foraging jobs.

buildings.name: Wood Gatherers' Camp
buildings.description: Must be next to forest. +3 Wood Gathering jobs.

buildings.name: Stone Gathering Site
buildings.description: Must be next to rock. +2 Stone Gathering jobs.

buildings.name: Storage Pit
buildings.description: +100 storage for food, wood and stone. Protects 40 food from spoilage.

buildings.name: Toolmaker's Shelter
buildings.description: +2 Crafting jobs. Crafters use wood and stone to make tools that speed up all gathering.

buildings.name: Community Circle
buildings.description: A ring of stones where the community decides together. +3 Research jobs. Needed for a stable village.

buildings.name: Village Hearth
buildings.description: The old campfire, now a permanent stone hearth at the village centre.

buildings.name: Fishing Weir
buildings.description: Stakes and woven traps in the shallows. Must touch the river or lake. +2 Fishing jobs.

buildings.name: Drying Rack
buildings.description: Meat and fish dry over a smoky fire. Protects 30 food from spoilage.

buildings.name: Elders' Lodge
buildings.description: A round lodge where elders teach. +3 Research jobs.

buildings.name: Longhouse
buildings.description: A long timber hall under thatch. Houses 8 people.

buildings.name: Daub House
buildings.description: Wattle walls sealed with clay and dung under a thick thatch. Houses 5 people in comfort.

buildings.name: Farm Field
buildings.description: Tilled strips of grain. +4 Farming jobs. Farms give most in autumn and nothing in winter.

buildings.name: Animal Pen
buildings.description: Goats and sheep behind a woven fence. +2 Foraging jobs and a new kind of food.

buildings.name: Granary
buildings.description: A raised store of clay pots. +150 storage and protects 80 food from spoilage.

buildings.name: Pottery Kiln
buildings.description: A domed clay kiln. +2 Crafting jobs.

buildings.name: Copper Smelter
buildings.description: A stone furnace and bellows. +2 Stone Gathering and +1 Crafting job.

buildings.name: Bronze Workshop
buildings.description: Moulds, crucibles and the first bronze tools. +3 Crafting jobs.

buildings.name: Hunter's Lodge
buildings.description: A lodge at the edge of the forest. Must touch the forest. +3 Hunting jobs (meat and hides).

buildings.name: Mine
buildings.description: A shaft into an ore vein at the foot of the mountains. Must touch ore. +3 Mining jobs.

buildings.name: Stone Cottage
buildings.description: A stone cottage with a tiled roof. Houses 6 people in comfort.

buildings.name: Town House
buildings.description: Two storeys: stone below, plaster above. Houses 10 people.

buildings.name: Tall Townhouse
buildings.description: Three storeys under a steep roof: the home of a burgher family. Houses 16 people.

buildings.name: Market Hall
buildings.description: A tiled hall where the valley trades. Big community boost and extra storage.

buildings.name: Watermill
buildings.description: A mill on the river. Must touch water. +3 Farming jobs.

buildings.name: Smithy
buildings.description: Forge, anvil and bellows. +4 Crafting jobs.

buildings.name: Church
buildings.description: A stone church with a bell tower. Huge community boost. +3 Research jobs (monks).

technologies.name: Improved Stone Tools
technologies.description: Sharper flaked tools. +25% foraging, wood and stone gathering.

technologies.name: Food Preservation
technologies.description: Drying and smoking. Halves food spoilage and +50% food storage.

technologies.name: Structural Weaving
technologies.description: Woven walls and lashings. Unlocks the Woven Shelter upgrade (houses 4).

technologies.name: Shared Labor
technologies.description: Organised work parties. +50% construction speed while 2 or more people work on Construction.

technologies.name: Permanent Settlement
technologies.description: The community commits to this place. Required to found a stable village.

technologies.name: Fishing
technologies.description: Bone hooks and woven traps. Unlocks the Fishing Weir. +5% foraging.

technologies.name: Hide Working
technologies.description: Scraped and smoked hides. Unlocks the Drying Rack. Food spoils 15% slower.

technologies.name: Oral Tradition
technologies.description: Stories carry knowledge between generations. Unlocks the Elders' Lodge. +15% research.

technologies.name: Longhouses
technologies.description: Long timber frames under thick thatch. Unlocks the Longhouse. Population grows 15% faster.

technologies.name: Agriculture
technologies.description: Sowing wild grain in tilled plots. Unlocks Farm Fields and Daub Houses.

technologies.name: Animal Husbandry
technologies.description: Penning goats and sheep. Unlocks the Animal Pen (a new kind of food).

technologies.name: Pottery
technologies.description: Fired clay pots keep grain dry. Unlocks the Granary and the Pottery Kiln. Food spoils 20% slower.

technologies.name: Copper Smelting
technologies.description: Green stones melt into copper in hot kilns. Unlocks the Copper Smelter. +15% stone gathering.

technologies.name: Bronze Working
technologies.description: Copper and tin make bronze: tools that never chip. Unlocks the Bronze Workshop. +20% to all gathering and farming.

technologies.name: Written Law
technologies.description: Marks on clay and wood that keep promises. The village is ready to ask a lord for a charter. +10% research.

technologies.name: Stone Masonry
technologies.description: Cut stone and lime mortar. Unlocks the Stone Cottage and the Town House. +15% stone gathering.

technologies.name: Ironworking
technologies.description: Iron from the red stones of the mountains. Unlocks the Smithy. +25% mining, +10% woodcutting.

technologies.name: The Watermill
technologies.description: The river turns the millstone. Unlocks the Watermill. +20% farming.

technologies.name: Craft Guilds
technologies.description: Masters, journeymen and apprentices. Unlocks the Market Hall. +15% crafting bonus.

technologies.name: Burgher Rights
technologies.description: Townsfolk with rights of their own. Unlocks the Tall Townhouse. Newcomers arrive 10% faster.

technologies.name: Monastic Orders
technologies.description: Monks who copy books and keep the calendar. Unlocks the Church. +20% research.

events.title: A Poor Foraging Season
events.text: Dry weather has left the berry bushes thin. For the next 4 minutes foraging yields 30% less. How will the community respond?

options.label: Ration food
options.tradeOff: Everyone eats 25% less for 4 min, but the population will not grow during that time.
options.legacyText: The community learned to share little in hard times.

options.label: Send everyone foraging
options.tradeOff: Foragers search further (+60% foraging for 4 min), but wood gathering is halved.
options.legacyText: Foragers mapped distant groves that later paths would follow.

options.label: Open the storage pit
options.tradeOff: Spend 15 stored food now. No other penalties — preparation pays off.
options.legacyText: Stored food carried the camp through a lean season — a lesson in planning ahead.

events.title: A Useful Stone Deposit
events.text: Scouts found a seam of fine flint on the eastern ridge. Opening it takes effort, but would serve the settlement for generations.

options.label: Open a quarry
options.tradeOff: Costs 10 food and 10 wood now. Stone gathering is permanently +30%.
options.legacyText: The Ridge Quarry was opened. Its stone will shape the village's future buildings.

options.label: Leave the ridge wild
options.tradeOff: No cost. The ridge stays rich in wild plants: foraging is permanently +10%.
options.legacyText: The eastern ridge was left untouched and became a cherished foraging ground.

events.title: Wandering Traders
events.text: A small band from downriver has arrived with flint and dried fish. They want food and timber in exchange.

options.label: Trade food for flint
options.legacyText: The first trade with the river people: food for fine flint.

options.label: Share a meal and stories
options.tradeOff: Give 25 wood for their fire, learn their ways: +25 knowledge.
options.legacyText: Strangers shared a fire and their stories became our own.

events.title: Wolves at Night
events.text: Howls circle the camp after dark. Wolves have found the smell of drying meat.

options.label: Raise a thorn fence
options.tradeOff: Costs 20 wood. The camp sleeps safely.
options.legacyText: A ring of thorns kept the wolves at bay.

options.label: Keep watch by the fire
options.tradeOff: No cost, but tired gatherers bring 20% less wood for 4 min.
options.legacyText: Watchers by the fire learned the voices of the night.

options.label: Let them be
options.tradeOff: Wolves raid the stores: everyone eats 30% more for 2 min.
options.legacyText: Wolves raided the stores, and the camp went hungry for a time.

events.title: The River Rises
events.text: Spring rain swells the river. Water creeps toward the lower stores.

options.label: Carry the stores uphill
options.tradeOff: Costs 15 wood for sledges. Nothing is lost.
options.legacyText: The people carried their stores uphill before the flood.

options.label: Trust the banks
options.tradeOff: Food spoils twice as fast for 3 min.
options.legacyText: The river took part of the stores — and taught respect for its seasons.

events.title: The First Harvest
events.text: The first fields have given grain. The people want to celebrate.

options.label: Hold a harvest feast
options.legacyText: The first harvest feast: songs that would be sung for a thousand years.

options.label: Store every grain
options.tradeOff: No cost, but some grumble: approval −4 for 4 min.
options.legacyText: Every grain went into the stores. The elders called it wisdom; the young called it meanness.

objectives.title: Secure the food supply
objectives.hint: Open People and assign idle residents to Foraging, or build a Foraging Camp, until food is rising.

objectives.title: Raise a new shelter
objectives.hint: Build a Shelter so the community has room to grow.

objectives.title: Stockpile wood and stone
objectives.hint: Build a Stone Gathering Site next to rock and assign stone gatherers.

objectives.title: Dig a Storage Pit
objectives.hint: A Storage Pit raises storage limits and protects food from spoiling.

objectives.title: Put people to work in three trades
objectives.hint: Assign residents to at least three different jobs in People.

objectives.title: Research an early technology
objectives.hint: Assign a researcher at the Campfire, then start a technology in Research.

objectives.title: Face the poor foraging season
objectives.hint: Choose how the community responds. Each option has a different trade-off.

objectives.title: Found a stable village
objectives.hint: Meet every requirement in Objectives, then found the village.

milestones.name: A Stable Village
milestones.description: The camp has become a permanent settlement.
milestones.legacyText: The campfire became the Village Hearth. Every later town centre will grow around this spot.

milestones.name: The Bronze Dawn
milestones.description: Fields, granaries and bronze: a new era begins.
milestones.legacyText: The village sowed its first fields and cast its first bronze. The Era of First Civilizations began.

milestones.name: The Charter
milestones.description: A lord grants the valley a charter: the village becomes a town.
milestones.legacyText: A lord's seal made the village a chartered town. The Middle Ages had come to the valley.

milestones.name: The Market Town
milestones.description: Craftsmen, a mill and a market: the town trades with the whole valley.
milestones.legacyText: The market bell rang for the first time. The town became the heart of the valley.

milestones.name: The Walled Town
milestones.description: Stone walls, a church tower and streets of tall houses.
milestones.legacyText: The church bell rang over walls of stone. The founders' town would stand for centuries.

regions.name: Home Clearing
regions.description: The riverside clearing where the camp stands.
regions.legacyText: The first clearing beside the river.

regions.name: Northern Forest
regions.legacyText: Scouts traced the river upstream through the northern forest.

regions.name: Western Woods
regions.description: Old trees west of the clearing.
regions.legacyText: Paths were cut into the western woods.

regions.name: Eastern Ridge
regions.description: Rocky high ground across the river.
regions.legacyText: Scouts crossed the river and climbed the eastern ridge.

regions.name: Southern Riverbank
regions.legacyText: The southern riverbank was explored — a future crossing point.

regions.name: Eastern Highlands
regions.description: Wind-cut uplands beyond the ridge, rich in stone.
regions.legacyText: Scouts climbed past the ridge and saw the highlands roll on toward the mountains.

regions.name: Southern Marsh
regions.description: Reed beds and pools where the river slows.
regions.legacyText: Scouts waded the southern marsh and found where the river widens into pools.

regions.name: Hills of Stone
regions.description: Open meadows and stony hills east of the ridge: good quarries.
regions.legacyText: Scouts crossed the ridge and found hills of good building stone.

regions.name: Iron Mountains
regions.description: Steep peaks with veins of ore at their feet.
regions.legacyText: Scouts came back from the mountains with green and red stones that melt in fire.

regions.name: Lake Country
regions.description: The river widens into a great lake full of fish.
regions.legacyText: Scouts followed the river south and found a lake as wide as the sky.

regions.name: Deep Forest
regions.description: Old woods south of the lake, rich in game.
regions.legacyText: Hunters returned from the deep forest with tales of giant elk.

regions.name: Southern Peaks
regions.description: Wild mountains beyond the lake, with ore in the scree.
regions.legacyText: The southern peaks were mapped for the first time.

decorations.name: Dirt Path
decorations.description: Beaten earth. People walk faster; workplaces beside it work 10% better.

decorations.name: Stone Road
decorations.description: Packed stones that never turn to mud.

decorations.name: Torch Post
decorations.description: A burning torch on a post: light at night.

decorations.name: Lantern Post
decorations.description: A clay lantern on a post.

decorations.name: Well
decorations.description: A stone-lined well at the heart of the village.

decorations.name: Totem
decorations.description: A carved totem of the founders.

decorations.name: Standing Stone
decorations.description: A single raised stone that marks the land as ours.

decorations.name: Cobbled Street
decorations.description: Cut stones set in sand: a proper town street.

decorations.name: Town Banner
decorations.description: A tall banner in the town's colours.

chapters.title: The Riverside Camp
chapters.story:
The winter in the north was the hardest anyone could remember. When the reindeer did not return, the families followed the river south, carrying fire in a clay pot.

After many days they came to a valley none of them had seen: a quiet river, a great lake beyond the trees, hills of grey stone and, far to the east, mountains that shine red at sunset.

You are the Founder. Make a camp by the water and keep everyone alive through their first year.
chapters.goal: Survive the first year and make the camp a stable village.
chapters.legacyText: The band survived its first year in the valley and the camp became a village.

chapters.title: The Stable Village
chapters.story:
The fire in the clay pot became a hearth of stone. Children are born who have never seen the north.

The elders say a village is more than huts: it needs paths between the homes, fences for the animals, light against the night and a place to remember the ancestors.

Lay out your village: roads, fences, lights and monuments, and give every family a trade.
chapters.goal: Shape the village: roads, beauty and skilled people.
chapters.legacyText: The village was laid out with paths, fences and the first monuments.

chapters.title: The Bronze Dawn
chapters.story:
Traders from the river people came with seeds of wheat and a blade that did not break: green-gold metal, born from stone and fire.

The red stones at the foot of the mountains are the same ore. To make bronze, the village must learn to sow fields, store grain and work the fire hotter than ever.

Scout the mountains, open a mine and bring the Bronze Dawn to the valley.
chapters.goal: Fields, a granary and bronze: open the Era of First Civilizations.
chapters.legacyText: Fields were sown and the first bronze was cast in the valley.

chapters.title: The Hillfort
chapters.story:
Bronze brought wealth, and wealth brings envy. Smoke has been seen beyond the southern peaks.

The founders' grandchildren look to the stony hills: a place that can be walled, with a view over the whole valley. A chieftain's hall, palisades and broad roads would make the village a hillfort.

Grow strong, wall the heart of the village and keep the mines working.
chapters.goal: A large, beautiful and well-defended settlement with a working mine.
chapters.legacyText: The village became a hillfort, walled and proud above the valley.

chapters.title: The Charter
chapters.story:
Centuries pass. The hillfort has become the largest settlement between the mountains and the sea, and its law-speakers can write.

A lord rides into the valley with a parchment and a seal. He will grant a charter: the village may become a town, with its own market and its own laws, if it is large, beautiful and well ordered.

Research Written Law, grow the town and win the charter. The Middle Ages begin.
chapters.goal: Win the lord's charter and open the Middle Ages.
chapters.legacyText: The charter was sealed and the valley entered the Middle Ages.

chapters.title: The Market Town
chapters.story:
With the charter came the right to hold a market. Merchants from beyond the mountains ask for iron, flour and cloth.

The town needs craftsmen: a smithy for the ore of the mountains, a watermill on the river, and a market hall where the valley meets.

Build stone houses, cobbled streets and the market town.
chapters.goal: A market hall, a smithy and a watermill in a town of 60.
chapters.legacyText: The market town traded with the whole valley.

chapters.title: The Walled Town
chapters.story:
Wealth draws danger as well as merchants. The council decides to raise walls of stone and a church whose tower can be seen from the mountain passes.

This is the last task of the founders' line in this age: a walled town that will stand for centuries.

Build the church, wall the town and fill its streets.
chapters.goal: A church, walls and a town of 80.
chapters.legacyText: The walled town was finished. The founders' line had built something that would outlive them all.

chapters.title: Beyond the Mountains
chapters.story: Ships, printing presses and maps of a world much larger than the valley. The next age is still being built.
